why: Partitioning into two groups with the smallest difference is subset sum over all targets at once: build the set of reachable subset sums, then the best split takes the reachable sum closest to total/2 from below, giving total - 2s.
hints: If one group sums to s, the other sums to total - s. What does the difference look like in terms of s?
The difference is total - 2s for s <= total/2, so you want the largest reachable subset sum not above total/2.
Compute reachability for sums 0..total/2 with the 0/1 subset-sum table (or a bitset), then scan down from total/2 to the first reachable sum. O(n * total).
pitfalls: Every element must be in a group; it is a partition, not a free choice of two subsets.
Only sums up to total/2 matter; the other half is the mirror image.
